details: The European Central Bank (ECB) increased its key interest rates by 25 basis points on Thursday, marking the first hike in almost three years. This decision comes as eurozone inflation climbed to 3.2% in May 2026, its highest level since September 2023, largely driven by surging energy costs stemming from ongoing geopolitical tensions and the conflict in the Middle East. The eurozone economy also contracted by 0.2% in the first quarter of 2026, raising concerns about stagflation. Policymakers indicated that persistent inflation risks now outweigh concerns about slowing economic growth.
title: ECB Raises Rates as Eurozone Inflation Intensifies Amid Geopolitical Tensions

details: Sam Bankman-Fried, the founder of the now-collapsed FTX cryptocurrency exchange, lost his bid on Friday to overturn his fraud conviction and 25-year prison sentence. A three-judge panel of the Manhattan-based 2nd U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals unanimously upheld the lower court's decision, stating that the prosecution's evidence against Bankman-Fried for stealing $8 billion from FTX customers was "conservatively stated, robust."
title: Sam Bankman-Fried's FTX Fraud Conviction and Sentence Upheld on Appeal

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has reached a staff-level agreement with Ukraine, paving the way for a $690 million disbursement under its Extended Fund Facility loan program. This funding comes despite delays in some structural reforms and a missed VAT benchmark. The IMF simultaneously lowered Ukraine's real GDP growth forecast for 2026 to between 1.0% and 1.6%, attributing the revision to the ongoing conflict in Ukraine and spillover effects from the Middle East.
title: IMF Greenlights Ukraine Aid Tranche, Citing War's Impact on Growth

details: The U.S. Federal Reserve is expected to maintain current interest rates as policymakers assess persistent inflation pressures. These pressures are stemming from elevated energy costs, ongoing tariffs, and increasing investment in artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure. AI-related spending is driving demand for materials, chips, and labor, contributing to broader inflation risks. Despite potential temporary inflation, new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh may favor a cautious approach, aiming to look through transient price increases.
title: US Fed to Weigh AI and Oil Inflation Pressures, May Hold Rates Steady

details: U.S. consumer sentiment showed an improvement in June, rising by four points from mid-May, primarily due to a moderation in gasoline prices. Average gas prices dropped from $4.50 to $4.10 per gallon. Despite this uptick, overall consumer sentiment remains at historically low levels, influenced by the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and persistently high inflation, which reached over 4% in May—a three-year high.
title: US Consumer Sentiment Rises in June as Gas Prices Ease, Inflation Still a Concern
